title: Fallback simulation sprint guide
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, field-friendly guide for running a 2–3 day fallback simulation sprint with sellers, platform SEs, and ops. The goal is to give sellers a rehearsal they can run with a technical contact so they can demonstrate — live — how Redwood handles failure modes that customers worry about: latency spikes, model regressions, quota exhaustion, region outages and private VPC failovers.

Audience:
- Field sellers (SEs) running pilots or POCs
- Platform/product sellers who need to show reliability & fallbacks
- Customer SREs/Platform engineers during technical evaluation

High-level outcomes (what we want by sprint end):
- A validated demo script that exercises at least 3 fallback paths
- Measured SLO impacts for each scenario (latency, error rate, failover time)
- An evidence packet (logs, traces, sample payloads) to attach to pilot decks and customer follow-ups
- List of action items for product/ops (gaps we hit)

Sprint overview (2-day ideal, flexible to 3):
Day 0 (prep, 2–4 hours)
- Identify customer persona and target flows (support chat, search rerank, summarization). Pick 1–2 representative prompts and a short evaluation set (10–20 samples).
- Select models & routes to exercise: hosted -> dedicated -> fallback-model-quantized
- Configure canary toggle (simple route policy pointing to fallback path) and record IDs
- Create a lightweight test harness (curl / node script) that can replay requests with controlled rate/size

Day 1 (simulation + measurement)
- Morning: run baseline traffic for 30–60 minutes to capture normal latency/throughput metrics
- Midday: inject scenario A (latency degradation on primary model) and observe auto-fallback route. Time-to-fallback, token delta, and customer-visible latency should be recorded.
- Afternoon: run scenario B (model quality regression) using seeded prompts that reveal a regress; route to verified variant and capture quality metrics (BLEU/ROUGE-ish or simple binary pass/fail per prompt).

Day 2 (edge cases + debrief)
- Morning: quota / admission control test — simulate capacity cap and validate reserved capacity fallback or graceful degradation messaging
- Midday: private/VPC failover test (if applicable) — simulate control-plane loss and verify cached responses / fallback policy behavior
- Afternoon: quick debrief, collect artifacts, draft one-pager for AE and a short clip (terminal + dashboard) for the customer recording

Roles & responsibilities (minimal):
- Seller/SE (owner of demo story): runs script, narrates tradeoffs, calls out expected user experience
- Ops/Platform engineer: toggles routing policies, monitors infra metrics, captures logs and traces
- Product/PM (optional): observes, notes product gaps and prioritization items
- Customer contact (if present): validates realism of scenarios and confirms acceptance criteria

Scenarios (concrete examples to copy-paste into scripts)
1) Latency spike on hosted model
- Trigger: artificial CPU/GPU contention on the host pool (ops route: tag pool as degraded) or throttle token generation in runtime PR environment
- Expected: Smart routing moves to dedicated or lower-latency variant in < 8s; streaming remains consistent; partial responses possible and retry semantics explained
- Capture: dashboard time series, request ids, trace spans, SLO delta %

2) Model regression (quality drop)
- Trigger: swap model version to a bad commit or a small, degraded quantized variant for a subset of traffic
- Expected: Redwood Optimize detects quality drop on eval set (or SE manually flips canary) and route falls back to verified variant or previous model snapshot
- Capture: before/after outputs for the eval set, human rating notes, automated metric change

3) Quota exhaustion / admission control
- Trigger: simulate burst of parallel requests to exceed reserved capacity and invoke admission policy or queueing behavior
- Expected: caller-facing errors or 429s with graceful degrade policy; cached responses or sampled latency increases depending on plan; seller explains pricing and reserved capacity tradeoffs
- Capture: error rates, queue length, tokens billed, sample client CLI output

4) Private deploy control-plane loss (for private deployments)
- Trigger: remove route to control plane or simulate private VPN loss (test in an isolated environment)
- Expected: private runtime continues to serve from local cache/KV for allowed prefixes and then gracefully fails to degraded model; audit logs contain event
- Capture: local runtime logs, cached response samples, audit log entry ids

Demo script snippets (short, copyable)
- "Start baseline: curl -X POST https://demo.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d @baseline.json -H 'Authorization: Bearer SEDEMO'"
- "Flip canary: ops: POST /admin/routing -d '{\"policy\":\"force-fallback\"}'"
- "Run regression eval: node eval-runner.js --set=pilot-prompts.json --model=canary"
(ops, please replace with real CLI commands prior to live run)

Artifacts to collect (required):
- Synthetic prompt set (10–20) as JSON
- Short video capture (screen + terminal) 60–120s of the most illustrative scenario
- Dashboards: per-route latency + token counts + error rate screenshots (time window annotated)
- Log bundle: request ids + trace ids for 3 failed requests per scenario
- Short one-pager (customer facing) summarizing behaviors and next steps

Seller talking points (concise)
- "Redwood routes traffic by policy — if your primary model or region degrades, the runtime will route to a compatible variant, preserving availability while our platform optimizes for quality and cost."
- "We can measure the user-visible latency and quality delta in your pilot and tune batching/caching to hit your SLOs without surprise billing."
- "Reserved capacity gives you predictable throughput; fallbacks protect you from spikes or backend task regression."

Acceptance checklist (what counts as success for the sprint)
- At least 3 fallback paths executed with captured artifacts
- Measured time-to-fallback under target (configurable per customer; default <10s)
- One curated slide and 60s recording for AE follow-up
- 3 action items with owners (product/ops/seller) captured in JIRA/Linear

Unresolved questions / TODOs (notes to self)
- Need a sanitized demo account that can be reused across regions without leaking customer data
- Verify CLI admin endpoints are safe to expose during a live POC (audit trail)
- Decide whether the recording should include sensitive logs or only summarized screenshots

Quick links / references:
- INF-7890: Canary simulation template (Jira)
- Confluence: Canary Simulation Templates page (linked above)
- Runtime PR with route toggle helper: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1452

Slack shorthand: #g2m-canary-sims for scheduling + postmortem artifacts

Notes to self (brainstorm fragments):
- Could we add a tiny UI in the Console for "simulate fallback" that creates synthetic traffic and runs the checklist automatically? Low effort: run replay + flip policy + screenshot dashboards.
- Consider a lightweight automated recorder that saves trace slices for 5 min pre/post-fallback to make evidence packets instant.
- Follow-up: pair with product to make an official AE kit (1 slide + 2 scripts + sample prompts)

End of guide — last pass should trim commands to safe runnable variants and add exact CLI values before sharing externally.

Feedback welcome: ping @claire.huang on Slack or leave comments in this doc.
